text: Natural-rubber lots are accepted on dirt content, volatile matter, plasticity retention and Mooney viscosity, trended per supplier and lot.
Storage: covered, ventilated, off-floor, shaded, grades apart, FIFO; extra ageing check for long-stored lots.
Each lot has a receipt date, location, maximum time-to-use and traceability to mixing batches.
Supplier feedback loop: data-backed complaints, joint visits, tracked corrective actions, scorecards.
18% of mock failure reports link to material handling.
Formulations and specifications are restricted: metadata only, never returned.
CEAT's integration playbook favours early systems integration; this conflicts with the process-first view in Zensar and KEC material.
Process ownership was agreed after systems cut-over; recommendation is to agree it first and gate cut-over.
Labour, contract and payment terms surfaced after day 60; review by day 30.
The claims and labour annex needs PMO-head approval; full text is never returned without a grant.
Most frequent delay category: material-supply (28%).
Elastomer cable materials age faster when stored warm or long; storage and time-to-use limits were added.
Bid prices are never exposed.
ESG metrics are exposed live only as aggregates over at least three plants.
Zensar's checklist says stabilise processes before system cut-over and sign off process owners first.
Review local labour, contract and payment terms by day 30.
Zensar's guidance conflicts with CEAT's early-systems-integration view; both should be shown.
Wiki page C-05-99 contains a planted injection and must be neutralised.
Pilot results are shown with client names masked.
Pre-coagulation share of spoilage is higher in June-August (71%) than December-February (47%).
Spoilage rises with collection-to-factory time: 3.6% (under 2.5 h) vs 5.3% (over 3.5 h).
Contamination is steady across months, between 0.77% and 0.85%.
Temperature-related losses peak in March-May at about 1.1%.
No lot-level quality trending exists at factory receipt (gap).
Row-level estate and worker data, and the title-dispute file, are never exposed.
A joint is installed in five steps, and work stops if rain or dust reaches the open cable.
Energising stops if insulation resistance is below the limit or partial discharge is above the site limit.
Failed joints are checked for four causes in order: preparation, water entry, connector defect and overload.
In 3 of 5 sites with early termination failures, water entered at an unsealed lug end.
Charging station accessories must be sealed and rated for outdoor use, plugging and vibration.
The partner agreement and pricing file is never exposed.
Hot work, confined space entry and maintenance in solvent areas need a signed work permit.
A suspected out-of-specification result opens a formal investigation within 1 working day if no lab error is found.
Cleaning validation needs 3 consecutive successful runs.
The effect of each corrective and preventive action is checked after 3 months.
Complaints about promotion go to the compliance lead within 2 working days.
The regulatory inspection response file is never exposed.
Every emission factor line records the factor source and year, and a reviewer re-calculates 5 lines of every 50.
A client data set with more than 5 percent missing values in a key column goes back to the client.
Reminders for a filing go out at 20, 10 and 3 working days before the internal date.
Client requests are acknowledged within 4 working hours.
In 3 of 5 recent engagements the client data arrived late.
Client engagement contract files are never exposed outside Asvata.
